transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, so… what’s been bothering me is that over the past year or so, I’ve been getting pulled off track really easily. Like, the smallest thing—a phone buzz, someone walking past my office, even just some random thought popping into my head—can take me away from what I’m doing before I even catch it.
How has your sleep been over the past several months—are you having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling rested when you wake up?
I’m not really sure it’s been a major issue. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern with sleep—some nights are better than others, but nothing specific is jumping out to me.
Thinking back, did you notice similar problems with distractibility or losing focus when you were a child or teenager, or is this something that only started within the past year?

No, looking back, it was there when I was a kid too. Teachers were always moving my seat because I’d talk too much, or I’d get up without asking. I remember blurting things out before they even finished asking the question. So it’s not completely new, I guess.
Would you say these attention and impulsivity issues are currently causing real problems for you at work or in your relationships, not just occasional annoyances?

Yeah, I’d say it’s starting to cause real problems. I’m still keeping up overall, but people at work are getting less patient with me when meetings or mentoring conversations go off track. And at home, it’s starting to wear on trust a bit when family plans don’t go the way they’re supposed to. It’s not totally falling apart, but it’s more than just an annoyance now.
Right now, do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still, or find yourself acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

Yeah, I do feel that a lot. If I’m supposed to sit still—like at a family dinner or one of the church volunteer meetings—I feel like there’s a motor running inside me. I’ll need to move around or keep my hands busy somehow. It’s hard to just sit there calmly.
Right now, do you still find yourself frequently interrupting conversations or blurting out responses before someone finishes speaking?

Yeah, I do. I catch myself cutting people off more than I should. Like I’ll jump into my wife’s conversations with her parents, or at work I’ll finish an employee’s thought before they’re done talking. I don’t mean it badly, but I can tell it rubs people the wrong way.
Do you often find yourself losing important items, forgetting appointments or tasks, or struggling to keep things organized on a regular basis?

Yeah, that happens, especially at home. I’ll tell my wife I’m going to call the insurance guy or pick something up for the house, and then a few days go by and she’ll ask me about it, and I realize I completely forgot. It’s not like I meant to ignore it—it just drops out of my head.
